item.title: 89 seconds to midnight: The cost of lost empathy
item.author: Adrian Liberto
item.description: Our greatest threat lies not only in nuclear arms or climate collapse but in the death of empathy itself. Unless we confront the four horsemen of exploitation, greed, colonialism and nationalism, nature will deliver the reckoning we refuse to face.

item.title: The Zionist experiment has failed: it must be abolished
item.author: Ariana Yekrangi
item.description: Far from an aberration, Israel’s genocide is the fulfilment of its design. The era of two-state fantasies is over. Only a single, secular republic offers justice.

item.title: Another US veto condemns Gaza to further genocide
item.author: Adrian Liberto
item.description: As Trump and Netanyahu cosy up in Washington again with fresh talks on Gaza, one thing is certain: there is no Israeli atrocity, however diabolical, that the US will not back. Here I pick at Dorothy Shea’s narrative after yet another US veto blocking moves to put an end to the genocide.

item.title: Beyond Trumpian Flirtations with Total Denuclearization
item.author: Omar Alansari-Kreger
item.description: Is Donald Trump to be taken seriously when openly speaking of denuclearization?

item.title: Looking away from Gaza will not assuage our conscience; only action will
item.author: Ariana Yekrangi
item.description: A genocide in Palestine is unfolding right before our eyes, a saga of despair and devastation that many in the West, cocooned in a bubble of comfort and convenience, choose to ignore.

item.title: Frail and Ambiguous Words: How Diplomacy Hinders Peace in Gaza
item.author: Ariana Yekrangi
item.description: In the UN's high-stakes negotiations, a pivotal linguistic duel over 'cessation' versus 'suspension' casts Gaza's fate into uncertainty.

item.title: ‘The Imagined Unity’: Understanding Nations, Nationalism and Their Bedrock
item.author: Alexander Stoney
item.description: How do the multifaceted processes of nation building shape our understanding and implications for the future of the United Nations?

item.title: '24 Years of Missed Opportunities': How the UN Failed to Secure Peace in the DRC
item.author: Alexander Stoney
item.description: As the UN's longest-standing peacekeeping mission faces a turbulent exit from the Democratic Republic of Congo, what were its critical failings, and what can the UN learn from them?
